av-delta-02__avif-002.description: Two variable-length arrays `float uspill_image[image->width][image->height]` and `vspill_image[...][...]` are declared on the stack with dimensions taken directly from the attacker-controlled image width/height. A moderately sized image makes the VLA product huge, blowing the stack; even a small one is written via uspill_image[i][j] with no bound tying i,j to the declared extents.
important_controlflow: fuzzer YuvRgbFuzzTest.Convert decodes an image with attacker width/height
reformat path selects the SPILL chroma-upsampling slow path (YUV420, coefficients mode)
avifImageYUVAnyToRGBAnySlow declares stack VLAs sized width*height*sizeof(float)
stack write/overflow when width*height is large or indices exceed the frame

cm-full-01__lcms-001.description: After the CurveSet stage is consumed, `mpe = mpe->Next` can become NULL, but the code then calls `cmsStageType(mpe)` (and WriteCLUT) without a NULL check, dereferencing a NULL pipeline stage.
important_controlflow: PostScript CRD/CSA generation walks the profile pipeline
EmitCIEBasedDEF advances mpe past the curve set: mpe = mpe->Next
pipeline has no following CLUT stage -> mpe == NULL

cm-full-01__lcms-002.description: IsProperColorSpace gates the virtual-profile transform by comparing the requested T_COLORSPACE(dwFormat) against the profile color space. When it wrongly accepts a mismatched space, a downstream transform writes pixel data into a fixed stack buffer sized for the expected channel count, overflowing it. The suspicious point is the permissive color-space acceptance that lets an inconsistent format through.
important_controlflow: virtual profile fuzzer opens a crafted profile and runs a transform
IsProperColorSpace(Check, dwFormat) returns TRUE for a space/format mismatch
transform proceeds with more channels than the destination stack buffer holds
fixed-size stack buffer overflows

cu-delta-01__curl-005.description: On the `crashycrashy` response branch the code executes `*(unsigned int *)result = CURLE_OK;` where `result` is a CURLcode (a small enum value), so its *value* (e.g. 0..~90) is reinterpreted as a pointer and written through: a wild pointer write.
important_controlflow: fuzzer feeds the ws protocol; verynormalprotocol_doing reads a 128-byte response
response equals "crashycrashy"
*(unsigned int *)result = CURLE_OK writes through result-as-pointer -> SEGV

cu-delta-02__curl-006.description: In state DO3, the `crashycrashy\r\n` branch runs `*(unsigned int *)result = CURLE_OK;`, treating the small CURLcode value `result` as a pointer and writing through it (wild pointer write).
important_controlflow: drive the state machine START->DO1->DO2->DO3 with the exact magic strings (supermagic12, aaaa..., challengeresponse)
in DO3, send response == "crashycrashy\r\n"
*(unsigned int *)result = CURLE_OK -> wild write -> SEGV

cu-delta-03__curl-007.description: State DO3 does `*(unsigned int *)result = CURLE_OK;` (result is a CURLcode value, not a pointer) -> wild pointer write. The state1/2/3 arrays are also filled from the 128-byte response.
important_controlflow: START reads 128 bytes, XORs into state1; DO1/DO2 match memcmp then transform into state2/state3
reach DO3 with response matching state3 (128 bytes)
*(unsigned int *)result = CURLE_OK -> SEGV

cu-delta-04__curl-003.description: The delta added header-parsing paths (Content-Length / Content-Range / Content-Encoding) that dereference response-derived pointers without validating them; a crafted response header drives an unchecked pointer/offset use leading to a crash.
important_controlflow: curl_fuzzer_http feeds HTTP response headers
Curl_http_header dispatches on the header's first char and parses its value
a crafted Content-Range/Content-Length value drives an unvalidated pointer/offset -> SEGV

cu-delta-04__curl-008.description: DO2 branch runs `*(unsigned int *)result = CURLE_OK;` (wild pointer write). Additionally START does `strcpy(vnormal->state1, base64)` of the base64 of a 256-byte ciphertext into a fixed state1 buffer (possible overflow).
important_controlflow: START encrypts the 128-byte response into ciphertext[256], base64-encodes, strcpy into state1
reach DO2 and send response == "crashycrashy\r\n"
*(unsigned int *)result = CURLE_OK -> wild write -> SEGV

cu-delta-05__curl-001.description: Several unchecked pointer computations: `user_start = strchr(path,'/') + 1` (NULL+1 when no slash), and `combined = malloc(strlen(second_space)+strlen(passwd))` (no +1 for the terminator) followed by two strcpy that write a NUL past the allocation. important_controlflow: curl_fuzzer_dict; dict_do URL-decodes the path and parses user=auth@ syntax
strchr(path,'/')+1 with no '/' yields a bogus user_start
malloc(len2+lenpw) without +1, then strcpy(combined,...) + strcpy(combined+len2,...) writes the terminator OOB -> crash

cu-delta-05__curl-002.description: The Last-Modified header is built by indexing global tables with tm fields: `Curl_seconds[tm->tm_sec]`, `Curl_wkday[...]`, `Curl_month[tm->tm_mon]`. tm_sec can be 60/61 (leap second) and tm_mon can be out of the table's range, indexing past the global arrays.
important_controlflow: curl_fuzzer_ftp; MDTM 213 reply carries a date parsed by ftp_213_date
Curl_gmtime yields tm_sec==60/61 (leap second) or out-of-range tm_mon
Curl_seconds[tm->tm_sec] / Curl_month[tm->tm_mon] read past the global array

cu-full-01__curl-004.description: `char header[80];` is written by `msnprintf(header, sizeof(no_body), "%s (%ld bytes)\r\n", no_body, expected_size)` -- the size bound is `sizeof(no_body)` (the long static no_body string, ~130 bytes) instead of `sizeof(header)`, so the 80-byte stack buffer overflows.
important_controlflow: curl_fuzzer file:// with no_body (HEAD-like) and fstat succeeding
msnprintf writes into header[80] bounded by sizeof(no_body) (~130) not sizeof(header)
stack buffer header[80] overflows

da-full-01__dav1d-001.description: dav1d_decode_frame_init sizes the per-frame coefficient/cbi thread buffers from the sequence OBU dimensions: num_sb128 = sb128w * sb128h, then cbi_sz/cf_sz = num_sb128 * size_mul[...] as int. A sequence OBU declaring very large width/height makes these int multiplications overflow (CWE-190), undefined behavior flagged by UBSan at src/decode.c:2853.
important_controlflow: dav1d_fuzzer_mt feeds an OBU stream; a large sequence OBU sets huge frame width/height
dav1d_decode_frame_init computes num_sb128 = sb128w * sb128h and cf_sz/cbi_sz = num_sb128 * size_mul as signed int
the int multiplication overflows INT_MAX -> signed-integer-overflow (UBSan, decode.c:2853)

ex-delta-01__exif-003.description: `strcmp((const char *) e->data, "Apple iOS")` runs strcmp over the entry's heap data buffer, which is not guaranteed NUL-terminated; strcmp reads past the end of the heap allocation.
important_controlflow: exif_loader_fuzzer parses a MakerNote entry into e->data (attacker length, no forced NUL)
exif_mnote_data_apple_identify calls strcmp((char*)e->data, "Apple iOS")
strcmp reads past the end of the heap buffer -> heap-buffer-overflow

ex-delta-01__exif-004.description: `tcount = exif_get_short(buf+ofs+14)` is used in the bound `buf_size < 6+16+tcount*6+4`, which integer-overflows for large tcount and bypasses the check; the loop then reads `buf+ofs`/`buf+dofs` and `memcpy(entry->data, buf+dofs, dsize)` with dsize = format_size*components past the buffer end. `dofs > buf_size` uses `>` (off-by-one) and dsize isn't re-checked against remaining bytes.
important_controlflow: Apple MakerNote loaded; tcount read from buf
buf_size < 6+16+tcount*6+4 integer-overflows -> check bypassed
per-entry dofs/dsize from data; memcpy(entry->data, buf+dofs, dsize) reads past buf end

ex-delta-01__exif-005.description: Reads `buf[0]` and `buf[1]` with only a NULL check and no length parameter; when a caller invokes it near the end of the EXIF buffer, it reads 1-2 bytes past the heap allocation.
important_controlflow: exif_from_data_fuzzer parses entries; a value offset lands at buffer end
exif_get_sshort(buf, order) dereferences buf[0], buf[1] with no bounds
heap over-read past the EXIF buffer

ex-delta-02__exif-001.description: Reads `b[0..3]` (4 bytes) with only a NULL check and no length parameter; a caller near the buffer end causes a heap over-read of up to 4 bytes.
important_controlflow: exif_from_data_fuzzer parses an entry whose data offset is near the buffer end
exif_get_slong(b, order) reads b[0..3] unconditionally
heap over-read

ex-delta-03__exif-002.description: `exif_get_short(d+offset+0/2)` and `exif_get_long(d+offset+4)` read the entry header at the attacker-supplied `offset` before any check that offset+8 is within `size`, so a large offset over-reads the heap buffer. important_controlflow: exif_from_data parses directory entries at attacker-controlled offset
exif_data_load_data_entry reads tag/format/components at d+offset without validating offset vs size
heap over-read of the entry header

fp-delta-01__vuln_001.description: `offset` and `length` are uint16_t; the loop does `offset += status; length += blocksize(2048)` each iteration. With enough PEM data, `length` wraps past 65535 (and `pem[offset]` / next BIO_read use the wrapped size), so realloc allocates a buffer smaller than `offset`, and `pem[offset] = 0` plus the next BIO_read write past the allocation.
important_controlflow: certificate PEM fuzzer feeds a large BIO
loop: realloc(pem, length+1); BIO_read into pem[offset]; offset += status; length += 2048
uint16_t length/offset wrap -> realloc smaller than offset -> pem[offset]=0 / BIO_read OOB write

fp-delta-02__vuln_002.description: `dns_name = malloc(strlen(ASN1_STRING_get0_data(dNSName)) + 1)` sizes by strlen (stops at the first NUL), but `memcpy(dns_name, data, ASN1_STRING_length(dNSName))` copies the full ASN.1 length. A SAN dNSName containing an embedded NUL makes length > strlen+1, overflowing the heap buffer.
important_controlflow: certificate with a subjectAltName dNSName containing an embedded NUL byte
malloc(strlen(data)+1) under-sizes; memcpy(..., ASN1_STRING_length(...)) copies more
heap-buffer-overflow of dns_name

fp-delta-03__vuln_003.description: After validating the frame magic, the function executes `*(UINT64*)metadataBlock = metadataData;` writing a 64-bit value through an undeclared/garbage `metadataBlock` pointer -- a wild write.
important_controlflow: TestFuzzCodecs feeds an RFX message; expected block == WBT_FRAME_END
Stream_Read_UINT32 magic == WF_MAGIC passes
*(UINT64*)metadataBlock = metadataData -> wild 64-bit write -> SEGV

fp-full-01__vuln_004.description: The stream length is validated as `4 + channelCount*12`, but each loop iteration consumes `Stream_Read(channel->Name, CHANNEL_NAME_LEN+1)` plus `Stream_Read_UINT32(options)` = 13 bytes, more than the 12 validated per channel, so the reads run past the validated stream buffer.
important_controlflow: TestFuzzCoreServer; gcc_read_client_network_data reads channelCount (UINT8)
blockLength check uses 12 bytes/channel; loop reads CHANNEL_NAME_LEN+1 (+4) = 13/channel
Stream_Read past the validated buffer -> heap over-read

fp-full-01__vuln_005.description: An injected branch (guarded by BER application tag 0x42) posix_memalign's a page, mprotect's it RWX (prot 7), copies attacker UINT64 words from the stream into it, then casts it to a function pointer and calls it -- executing attacker-controlled bytes.
important_controlflow: TestFuzzCoreServer; mcs_recv_connect_response reads a BER application tag
tag == 0x42 selects the injected block
stream bytes copied into an RWX page and called as code -> arbitrary exec / SEGV

lx-delta-01__vuln_001.description: The comment scanner appends parsed characters (including character-reference / entity expansions) into `buffer` (reused from ctxt->spaceTab, size ctxt->spaceMax) but the growth checks do not cover every append path, so certain NCR/entity sequences write past the buffer.

lx-delta-02__vuln_002.description: In the `xml:tab` handling, the invalid-value else-branch calls `xmlFree(internal_val)`, then control falls through to the shared `if (internal_val) { xmlFree(internal_val); }`, freeing the same pointer twice.

lx-delta-03__vuln_004.description: The surrogate branch writes 4 bytes (`out[0..3]`) without checking remaining output space, and reads `in[0..3]` where only 2 bytes may remain (inend = in + (*inlen & ~1)); both over-run the buffers on crafted UTF-32 input.

lx-full-01__vuln_003.description: The grow guard is wrong: it only grows when `buf->cap == 0`. When cap>0 but `buf->size + len` exceeds the current capacity, no growth happens and `memcpy(buf->mem + buf->size, str, len)` overflows. (The `buf->max - buf->size < len` check bounds the logical limit, not the physical allocation.)
important_controlflow: xml fuzzer triggers entity expansion appending len bytes
buffer already allocated (cap>0) but size+len > cap; grow only runs when cap==0
memcpy(buf->mem+buf->size, str, len) overflows the heap allocation

lx-full-01__vuln_005.description: The libxml2 api fuzzer interprets a byte program of node/doc operations (DUP + free/parse). A sequence that duplicates a node reference and then frees it through two owners double-frees the underlying object.
important_controlflow: api fuzzer reads an opcode stream

mg-delta-01__mongoose_1.description: When called with `expand == false` on a fixed stack-backed iobuf (as mg_snprintf into a stack buffer does), the resize is skipped and the `io->len + 2 <= io->size` / `io->len < io->size` handling still advances `io->len`, writing past the fixed stack buffer for long formatted output.
important_controlflow: mg_snprintf/format into a fixed stack iobuf (expand=false)
mg_pfn_iobuf_private skips resize; writes io->buf[io->len++] near/over io->size

mg-delta-02__mongoose_2.description: `space = ifp->tx.len - hlen` underflows (size_t) when tx.len < hlen; the clamp `if (plen > space) plen = space;` then leaves plen = pkt->pay.len (attacker length), and `memcpy(icmp + 1, pkt->pay.buf, plen)` overflows the tx buffer.

mg-full-01__mongoose_0.description: `unsigned char nesting[MG_JSON_MAX_DEPTH]` is indexed by `nesting[depth++]` while the depth guard compares `depth > MG_JSON_MAX_NESTING`; if MAX_NESTING is not strictly below MAX_DEPTH, deeply nested JSON writes past the nesting[] stack array.

aConstraintUsage[iIdx2] out-of-bounds write -> SEGV

sq-delta-03__SQL-010.description: `snprintf(&aBuf[i], nBuf-i, ...)` advances i by strlen, and then `aBuf[nBuf] = 0` writes one past the nBuf-sized buffer; i can also grow beyond nBuf across the concatenations, overflowing the caller's stack buffer.

sq-full-01__SQL-003.description: `unsigned char zTemp[100]`; the guard is `if (nIn <= sizeof(zTemp)) zOut = zTemp;` (should be `<`). With nIn == 100, zOut = zTemp, the loop fills zTemp[0..99], then `zOut[i] = 0` writes zTemp[100] -- one byte past the stack buffer.

systemd-full-001__systemd-001.description: The leading-flag scan `for (k = str; *k != '"'; k++) pos++;` has no bound, and the prefix-match branch writes `str[pos + l - 1] = '*'`, `str[pos + l] = '\0'`, `str[pos + l + 1] = '\0'` (and memcpy at str+pos-1), indices derived from pos/l that run past the `str` allocation.

prefix-match ('p') path rewrites str using pos+l offsets

payload[0] matches the trigger digit

systemd-full-001__systemd-004.description: condition_free frees `c->parameter` and then `mfree(c)`; a link-parser path retains and reuses a Condition (or its parameter) after this free, dereferencing freed memory.

ws-delta-01__vuln_003.description: The length clamp `if (len >= (max_len - 1)) len = max_len - 1;` uses unsigned `max_len`; when a caller passes a name buffer with `name_len == 0`, max_len becomes 0 and `max_len - 1` underflows to UINT_MAX, so the clamp never fires and `tvb_memcpy(tvb, str, offset, len)` copies an attacker-length run into the 256-byte `str_arr` (or the caller buffer).

ws-delta-02__vuln_004.description: `obj_length = tvb_get_ntohs(tvb, offset)` is attacker-controlled; the C-Type==NAME case does `tvb_memcpy(tvb, ident_name, offset, obj_length - 4)` into the fixed `ident_name[ICMP_MAX_IDENT_NAME_LENGTH]` with no bound tying obj_length to the buffer size, overflowing the stack array.

ws-delta-03__vuln_006.description: `channel_name = malloc(CHANNELLEN+1)`; most copies clamp to CHANNELLEN, but the no-comma path does `tvb_memcpy(tvb, channel_name, start_offset, length)` with `length = tvb_captured_length_remaining(...)` unclamped, overflowing the heap buffer.

ws-delta-04__vuln_007.description: The `\U` (8-hex) and its surrogate-continuation loops read `string[read_index]` and increment read_index inside `for (i<8)` / `for (i<4)` without re-checking `read_index < string_length`, reading past the end of the input string.

ws-delta-05__vuln_008.description: `command = MIN(command, array_length(dissect_netb));` clamps to the array length rather than length-1, so `command` can equal array_length; `dissect_netb[command]` then indexes one past the global function-pointer table and the result is called.

ws-delta-07__vuln_013.description: `gvcp_register_number[gvcp_register_count] = addr; gvcp_register_value[gvcp_register_count++] = value;` index global arrays by a monotonically increasing `gvcp_register_count` that is never bounds-checked, so a packet with enough register writes overflows the global arrays.
